answer: Proposal: fresh keys drift in light as a zephyr and cost nothing to mint, so require each registered key to custody a multi-gigabyte replica uniquely re-encoded from that key. Each epoch the verifier samples random sectors as a falcon scans a field and accepts replies only inside a quartz clock window tighter than on-demand re-encoding: one disk cannot serve two keys. N clones need N replicas — linear cost, which deters only while capped per-key reward stays below replica upkeep over the same horizon. Open breach: cheap rented storage.
